scope: Owned synthetic SQL records; offline comparison, not a production SLA.
timing: perf_counter_ns around direct store check + recording through SQL commit. Warmups, session/receipt creation, SQL inspection, cleanup, HTTP and controlled interleaving waits excluded. All outcomes retained in sample denominator; nearest-rank percentiles. Strategy order rotates each round; fresh identical state for each normal request.
concurrency: Independent connections in threads, synchronized after the separate-check opportunity. Source edit is committed before simultaneous writes in edit_after_check. All strategies deduplicate the same key. check_then_act checks before its deduplication. One separately recorded same-key retry after the wave for SQL operational failures only. The lock_timeout_retry workload deliberately holds a real SQL lock until first-wave timeouts.
limitations: Five controlled workloads, not arbitrary schedule exploration or sustained load.
Normal request samples share a host and database pool; they are not independent production trials.
Historical replay is not a new stale write. It does not revalidate the old answer.
No external side effects, multi-host guarantee, model quality or applicant authorship claim.
